formula: circumference ~ SSlogis(age, Asym, xmid, scal), tree-specific Asym (logistic growth)
notes: NONLINEAR: logistic growth curve (SSlogis) of trunk circumference in age, tree-specific asymptote. Help page fits nlmer(circumference ~ SSlogis(age) ~ Asym|Tree) in a dontrun block; Pinheiro & Bates 2000. Tree is the grouping.

formula: distance ~ age * Sex + (age | Subject)
notes: Help page gives no model (str only). Recalled Pinheiro & Bates 2000 Appendix A.17 (Potthoff & Roy growth curves): distance grows linearly with age, Sex main effect and age:Sex, random intercept and age slope by Subject. Subject is an ordered-factor grouping id (declare nothing).

formula: follicles ~ sin(2*pi*Time) + cos(2*pi*Time) + (1 | Mare)
notes: Help page gives no model (str only). Recalled P&B 2000 Appendix A.18: follicle counts modelled on harmonics of the scaled cycle Time with mare random effects and AR(1) errors. follicles are counts (response_type count); Mare is an ordered grouping id. Time entered as sin/cos.

formula: Thickness ~ Source + (1 | Lot/Wafer)
notes: Help page describes a variance-components design (Littell et al. 1996 p.155; P&B A.20): oxide thickness over 8 lots, 3 wafers per lot, 3 sites per wafer, 2 sources; no formula on page. Recalled nested Lot/Wafer variance components. RULE GAP: Source is a 2-level design factor; filed as a fixed covariate rather than a grouping factor (a 2-level random effect is substantively weak). Site indexes the 3 within-wafer replicates (left as an unused column).

formula: deltaBP ~ four-parameter logistic in log(dose) (SSfpl), Treatment shifts the curve, rabbit random effects
notes: NONLINEAR: four-parameter logistic dose-response of deltaBP in log(dose), Treatment shifts the curve, rabbit random effects. Help page cites Ludbrook 1994 and Venables & Ripley 1999 section 8.8 (no formula on page); 5 rabbits, placebo vs MDL 72222 crossover. Run (=Rabbit:Treatment, 10 curves) ignored as a composite id; Rabbit and Run are ordered ids.

formula: conc ~ one-compartment IV PK, first-order elimination (dose, time); subject-specific clearance and volume; Wt and Apgar covariates
notes: NONLINEAR: one-compartment IV PK with first-order elimination, inputs dose and time, subject-specific clearance and volume, birth-weight (Wt) and Apgar covariates. Help page describes a neonatal phenobarbital PK study (Grasela & Donn 1985; Davidian & Giltinan 1995 section 6.6; P&B A.23), str only. Dosing rows (conc NaN) dropped by the measurer. Apgar ignored as the alternate of ApgarInd (pilot ignored-copy rule); Subject is an ordered grouping id.

formula: pixel ~ day + I(day^2) + (1|Dog:Side) + (day|Dog)
notes: Help page fits lmer(pixel ~ day + I(day^2) + (1|Dog:Side) + (day|Dog)): CT-scan pixel intensity over days, dog random slope in day and a dog-side intercept. Dog:Side is the composite whole-unit term.

formula: conc ~ one-compartment oral PK, first-order absorption and elimination (dose, time); subject clearance with weight, age, creatinine clearance, glycoprotein, ethanol covariates
notes: NONLINEAR: one-compartment oral PK with first-order absorption and elimination, inputs dose and time, subject-specific clearance with weight, age, creatinine-clearance, alpha-1-glycoprotein and ethanol covariates. Help page describes routine clinical quinidine PK (Verme et al. 1992; Davidian & Giltinan 1995 section 9.3; P&B A.25), str only. Dosing rows (conc NaN) dropped. Creatinine declared ordered covariate; Subject grouping id. Height, Race, Smoke, Heart left as unused columns.

formula: travel ~ 1 + (1 | Rail)
notes: Help page fits lmer(travel ~ 1 | Rail): one-way random-effects (variance components) model of ultrasonic travel time by rail. Rail is an ordered grouping id.

formula: weight ~ Treatment + sex + Lsize + (1 | Litter)
notes: Help page gives no model (str only). Recalled West, Welch & Galecki (WWGbook) / P&B rat-pup example: weight on litter-level Treatment (ordered Control<Low<High), pup sex and litter size Lsize, litter random intercept (with variance heterogeneity). Treatment declared ordered covariate; Litter is the grouping.

formula: cAMP ~ four-parameter logistic dose-response in conc, run-specific random effects (bioassay)
notes: NONLINEAR: sigmoid (four-parameter logistic) dose-response of cAMP in conc, run-specific random effects. Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, no model or section; rendered from the relaxin-bioassay design (dose conc, readout cAMP, 9 assay runs). Run is an ordered grouping id. Low confidence: no cited model.

formula: conc ~ compartmental IV-infusion PK (Rate, Amt, Time); subject-specific clearance and volumes; age, sex, height, weight covariates
notes: NONLINEAR: compartmental IV-infusion PK (inputs Rate, Amt, Time), subject-specific clearance and volumes, with age/sex/height/weight covariates (Minto remifentanil model). Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, str. Dosing/infusion rows (conc NaN) dropped. ID ignored as numeric alternate of Subject; BSA and LBM ignored as derived from Ht/Wt (pilot ignored-copy rule); Subject is an ordered grouping id.

formula: weight ~ SSlogis(Time) logistic growth; Variety and Year modify growth parameters; plot random effects
notes: NONLINEAR: logistic growth curve (SSlogis) of average leaf weight in Time, Variety (F/P genotype) and Year modifying growth parameters, plot-specific random effects. Help page cites Davidian & Giltinan 1995 1.1.3 and P&B A.27, commented nlsList(SSlogis) example. Plot is the grouping.

formula: logSize ~ days + (days | Tree), trees nested in plot: (1 | plot/Tree)
notes: Help page gives no model (str only). Recalled Diggle, Liang & Zeger 1994 Example 1.3 / P&B A.28: log tree size grows with days, tree random effects nested in plot (ozone vs normal atmosphere, not a column here). logSize is already the logged response (no raw size column); Tree nested in plot.

formula: conc ~ one-compartment PK in Time; subject-specific parameters; two formulations (tetrachel vs tetracyn) crossover
notes: NONLINEAR: one-compartment PK of tetracycline (input Time), subject-specific parameters, two Formulations (tetrachel vs tetracyn) compared in a crossover. Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, str; rendered from the PK design. Subject is an ordered grouping id. Low confidence: no cited model or section.

formula: conc ~ one-compartment PK in Time; subject-specific parameters; two formulations (Berkmycin vs tetramycin) crossover
notes: NONLINEAR: one-compartment PK of tetracycline (input Time), subject-specific parameters, two Formulations (Berkmycin vs tetramycin) compared in a crossover. Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, str; rendered from the PK design. Subject is an ordered grouping id. Low confidence: no cited model or section.

formula: conc ~ SSfol(Dose, Time) first-order one-compartment oral PK; subject-specific lKe, lKa, lCl
notes: NONLINEAR: first-order one-compartment oral PK (SSfol) in Dose and Time, subject-specific lKe, lKa, lCl. Help page fits nls(conc ~ SSfol(Dose, Time)) per subject and cites Davidian & Giltinan 1995 sections 5.5/6.6 and P&B A.29. All rows are measured (no separate dosing rows). RULE GAP: the nonlinear within-curve inputs (Dose, Time) are named in the formula words only; covariates is left blank for subject-level covariates (none here) because the prompt does not say where the time/dose axis belongs.

formula: current ~ poly(voltage) + (1 | Wafer/Site) (I-V characteristic rendered as a grouped polynomial)
notes: Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, str. Rendered from the design: current-voltage (I-V) characteristic of analog MOS circuits, 10 wafers by 8 sites, current on voltage (nonlinear/polynomial) with wafer and site-within-wafer random effects. Low confidence: no cited model or section; the voltage effect is nonlinear, filed as a grouped polynomial.

formula: DryMatter ~ Moisture + fertilizer + (1 | Tray)
notes: Help page (P&B 2000) gives data only, str. Rendered from the design: greenhouse dry-matter yield over 12 trays, Moisture constant within a tray and fertilizer varying within, tray random intercept. Low confidence: no cited model. Tray is an ordered grouping id.

formula: yield ~ variety + (1 | Block) with spatial correlation on latitude/longitude
notes: Help page gives no model (str only). Recalled P&B 2000 Wheat2 spatial-correlation example: yield on variety (56 cultivars) with block random intercept and spatial correlation on latitude/longitude (coordinates left as unused columns; the reader loses the correlation structure). Block is an ordered grouping id.

formula: effort ~ Type + (1 | Subject)
notes: Help page fits lmer(effort ~ Type + (1|Subject)): Borg-scale effort to rise from 4 stool types, subject random intercept (balanced within-subject design). P&B A.9.
